events.title: The Council of Ephesus proclaims Mary Mother of God
events.shortBlurb: The third ecumenical council condemned Nestorius and confessed the Virgin Mary as Theotokos, the God-bearer…
body: The third ecumenical council opened at Ephesus on 22 June 431 under the presidency of St. Cyril of Alexandria, to judge the teaching of Nestorius, Patriarch of Constantinople, who denied to the Virgin Mary the title Theotokos, “Mother of God.” The council condemned Nestorius and confessed that the child born of Mary is truly God, so that she is rightly called God-bearer.

The people of Ephesus, who held the Mother of God in great honor, are said to have escorted the bishops home with torches and acclamation. The council's definition safeguarded the unity of the person of Christ and remains a foundation of Catholic devotion to Our Lady.

events.title: The martyrdom of St. John Fisher
events.shortBlurb: The Bishop of Rochester was beheaded for refusing to acknowledge Henry VIII as head of the Church in England…
body: John Fisher, Bishop of Rochester and a renowned scholar, was the only English bishop to refuse the oath acknowledging King Henry VIII as Supreme Head of the Church in England and denying the authority of the pope. Imprisoned in the Tower of London, he was created a cardinal by Pope Paul III while a captive.

On 22 June 1535 he was beheaded on Tower Hill, a fortnight before his friend St. Thomas More met the same death. Both were canonized by Pope Pius XI in 1935 as martyrs for the unity of the Church and the primacy of the See of Peter.

events.title: The abjuration of Galileo
events.shortBlurb: Galileo Galilei was made to renounce the Copernican doctrine before the Roman Inquisition…
body: On 22 June 1633, before the tribunal of the Roman Inquisition, Galileo Galilei was compelled to abjure the teaching that the earth moves about the sun, which the judges held to be contrary to Scripture. Found “vehemently suspected of heresy,” he was sentenced to imprisonment, soon commuted to house arrest, and his Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems was placed on the Index.

The episode became a byword for the supposed conflict of faith and science. Centuries later the Church acknowledged the errors of Galileo's judges; in 1992 Pope St. John Paul II, drawing on the study of a papal commission, declared the case a painful misunderstanding and honored Galileo's genius.
